parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Prove by mathematical induction that $u_n$ is an integer for every $n\in\mathbb Z^+$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the smallest positive integer $n$ for which $u_n>10^6$.

questions.answerSummary: $u_n$ is integral by induction; first $n$ above threshold is6.

steps.text: The base case and induction step establish the result for all positive integers.

questions.stem: This question concerns sketches from qualitative information. Numerical coordinates of any intercept not specified need not be calculated. Draw each sketch on a separate set of axes.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The differentiable function $f$ is even and tends to $3$ as $x\to\pm\infty$. It satisfies $f(0)=-3$, $f(\pm1)=1$ and $f(\pm2)=4$. Its derivative is positive for $x<-2$ and $0<x<2$, negative for $-2<x<0$ and $x>2$, and zero only at $-2,0,2$. Sketch a possible graph of $y=f(x)$, showing its stationary points and horizontal asymptote.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: The function $g$ is differentiable for $x\ne1$. Its limits are $g(x)\to-2$ as $x\to-\infty$, $g(x)\to1$ as $x\to+\infty$, $g(x)\to-\infty$ as $x\to1^-$ and $g(x)\to+\infty$ as $x\to1^+$. It has $g\prime(x)>0$ for $x<0$ and $x>2$, and $g\prime(x)<0$ for $0<x<1$ and $1<x<2$. The only stationary points are at $x=0$ and $x=2$, with $-1<g(0)<0$ and $0<g(2)<1$. Sketch a possible graph, showing all asymptotes and stationary points. The exact stationary ordinates are not required.

questions.answerSummary: Part(a): two maxima and one minimum, asymptote $y=3$. Part(b): one maximum and one minimum, asymptotes $x=1$, $y=-2$ and $y=1$.

steps.text: Even graph, with correct labelled given points and symmetry.
Local minimum at $(0,-3)$, with branches consistent with derivative signs.
Vertical asymptote $x=1$, horizontal asymptotes $y=-2$ on left and $y=1$ on right.
Correct branches approaching $-\infty$ and $+\infty$ at the indicated sides of1.
One local maximum at $x=0$, with negative ordinate between-1and0.
One local minimum at $x=2$, with positive ordinate between0and1, and correct increasing/decreasing intervals.

questions.stem: Points $A$ and $B$ are fixed with $AB=20$. A ray starts at $B$ and makes an angle of $45^\circ$ with $BA$. The point $X$ may lie anywhere on this ray other than $B$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the exact value of $BX$ when $AX$ is as small as possible.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the exact value of $BX$ when $AX=20$.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: When $AX=17$, find both possible values of $BX$.

steps.text: The shortest distance is perpendicular to the ray, so $BX=20\cos45^\circ$.

steps.text: Equating real and imaginary parts gives $5a-b=25$ and $12a+96=0$.

questions.stem: The function $\arctan$ takes its principal values in $(-\pi/2,\pi/2)$. Angles are in radians.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Give a counterexample to the claim that $\arctan(\tan x)=x$ for every real $x$ for which $\tan x$ exists.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Prove that $\arctan x+\arctan(1/x)=\pi/2$ for every $x>0$.

steps.text: $\tan A\tan B=1$, so $\cos(A+B)=\cos A\cos B(1-\tan A\tan B)=0$.
As $0<A+B<\pi$, the only possible zero of cosine is $A+B=\pi/2$.

questions.stem: The line $l_1$ has Cartesian equation $\dfrac{x+16}{-5}=\dfrac{y+4}{-7}=z$. The line $l_2$ passes through $A(3,4,1)$ and $B(0,6,0)$. Let $C=(-11,3,-1)$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find a vector equation for $l_2$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Show that $l_1$ and $l_2$ meet, and find their point of intersection $P$.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Show that the lines are perpendicular.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Show that $C$ lies on $l_1$.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: The point $D$ is the reflection of $C$ in the line $l_2$. Find $D$.

parts.label: f
parts.prompt: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane containing both lines.

steps.text: These values satisfy all three components, so the lines intersect.
Take the dot product of direction vectors.
$CP$ is perpendicular to $l_2$, so $P$ is the midpoint of $CD$.
Use a point on the plane, such as $(3,4,1)$.

questions.stem: Let $f(x)=\sqrt{1+x}+\sqrt{1-x}$, $-1\le x\le1$. Its graph has endpoints $A$ at $x=-1$ and $B$ at $x=1$. Let $R$ be the region bounded by this graph, the two coordinate axes and the line $x=1$, in the first quadrant.

parts.label: a(i)
parts.prompt: Find the exact $y$-coordinate of $A$.

parts.label: a(ii)
parts.prompt: State the range of $f$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: The horizontal line $y=k$ is tangent to the graph. Find $k$.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: The line $OB$, where $O$ is the origin, has gradient $m$. Find $m$.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find all real $k$ for which the line $y=kx$ does not meet the graph.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: Find the exact area of $R$.

parts.label: f
parts.prompt: Find the volume generated when $R$ is rotated through $2\pi$ radians about the $x$-axis.

parts.label: g
parts.prompt: Find the volume generated when $R$ is instead rotated through $2\pi$ radians about the $y$-axis. Show your method.

steps.text: The minimum is $\sqrt2$ at either endpoint.
The maximum is $2$ at $x=0$, so $\sqrt2\le y\le2$.
For $x>0$, the continuous ratio $f(x)/x$ takes exactly $[\sqrt2,\infty)$; for $x<0$ it takes $(-\infty,-\sqrt2]$. Hence slopes strictly between these ranges cannot meet the curve.
The inequalities are strict because equality gives an endpoint intersection.
Split into cylinder height $\sqrt2$, radius1, and upper cap.
Total $V=\pi(16+8\sqrt2)/15\approx5.72$ cubicunits. Equivalent shell integration is valid.

questions.stem: Points $B,A,Q$ lie in this order on a horizontal line, with $BA=1$ and $AQ=2$. The point $P$ is vertically above $Q$ with $QP=x>0$. Let $\alpha=\angle PAQ$ and $\beta=\angle PBQ$. Define $f(x)=x/(6+x^2)$ for $x>0$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Express $\alpha$ and $\beta$ in terms of $x$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Show that $\alpha-\beta=\arctan\left(\dfrac{x}{6+x^2}\right)$.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the exact coordinates of the maximum point of $y=f(x)$, justifying your answer.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: The graph $y=f(x)$ has a point of inflexion at $x=p$, where $p>0$. Find $p$ exactly.

parts.label: e(i)
parts.prompt: Find the maximum value of $\angle APB$ in degrees.

parts.label: e(ii)
parts.prompt: Find both possible values of $x$ for which $\angle APB=10^\circ$.

questions.answerSummary: Maximum at $x=\sqrt6$; inflexion $3\sqrt2$; maximumangle11.5degrees;10degrees occurs at1.41or4.26.

steps.text: The derivative changes from positive to negative there.
The positive root is $p=\sqrt{18}=3\sqrt2$, and the numerator changes sign there.
$\angle APB=\alpha-\beta$, maximized when $f(x)$ is maximal because arctangent is increasing.
